cat: Capital budgeting and cost of capital
name: NPV of single cash flow
description: Computes the net present value of one future cash flow against an initial investment, using cf/(1 + r)^t − c0. It discounts the future cash flow to today and subtracts the upfront cost.
notes: Enter the discount rate r as a decimal per period, matching the period of t. A positive result suggests the cash flow more than repays the initial investment.

cat: Capital budgeting and cost of capital
name: Payback period
description: Divides the initial investment by the annual cash flow to find the payback period, the number of years needed to recover the original outlay from equal yearly inflows.
notes: Assumes constant annual cash flow and ignores the time value of money and any inflows after payback. Use consistent currency for investment and cash flow.

cat: Capital budgeting and cost of capital
name: WACC
description: Computes the weighted average cost of capital by blending the cost of equity and the after-tax cost of debt according to their weights in the capital structure. It gives the overall required return that funds a firm's assets.
notes: Rates and weights are decimals, and the equity and debt weights should sum to 1. Only debt gets the (1 − tax) shield, reflecting the tax deductibility of interest.

cat: Capital budgeting and cost of capital
name: Weighted Average Cost of Capital (WACC)
description: Blends the cost of equity and the after-tax cost of debt, each weighted by its share of total financing, to give the firm's overall required return. It is the discount rate used to value the whole company.
notes: Weights should ideally use market values and sum to 1. The debt term is multiplied by (1 minus tax rate) to reflect the tax deductibility of interest; rates are entered as decimals.

cat: Capital budgeting and cost of capital
name: Net Present Value (2 Periods)
description: Discounts two years of cash flows back to today and subtracts the initial investment, giving the net present value of a simple project. A positive result means the project adds value at the given discount rate.
notes: Cash flows are assumed to arrive at the end of years 1 and 2, and the initial investment occurs now (time zero). Enter the discount rate as a decimal; this two-period form only handles c1 and c2.

cat: Capital budgeting and cost of capital
name: Profitability Index
description: Divides the present value of a project's future cash flows by its initial investment, showing the value created per unit of money invested. A value above 1 indicates the project is expected to add value.
notes: The numerator should already be discounted to present value. A PI above 1 corresponds to a positive NPV; it is useful for ranking projects when capital is limited.

cat: Capital budgeting and cost of capital
name: Equivalent Annual Cost (Capital Recovery)
description: Converts a present-value cost into a level annual payment over n periods using the capital recovery factor, given the present value and period rate. It spreads a lump-sum cost into equal yearly amounts.
notes: Useful for comparing assets with different lifespans on an annual basis. Payments are assumed at period end; enter the rate as a decimal, and the result carries the same currency as the present value.

cat: Capital budgeting and cost of capital
name: Free Cash Flow to Firm
description: Computes cash available to all investors by taking after-tax operating profit (EBIT times one minus tax), adding back depreciation, and subtracting capital expenditure and the increase in net working capital.
notes: Depreciation is added back because it is a non-cash expense already deducted in EBIT. Enter the tax rate as a decimal; nwc is the change in working capital, not its level.

cat: Capital budgeting and cost of capital
name: Free Cash Flow to Firm (FCFF)
description: Computes free cash flow to the firm from after-tax operating profit plus depreciation, less capital expenditure and the increase in working capital, EBIT*(1-t) + dep - capex - dwc. It is the cash available to all capital providers.
notes: t is the tax rate as a decimal, and dwc is the increase in net working capital (a decrease would add cash). All amounts should share the same currency and period.

cat: Capital budgeting and cost of capital
name: Free Cash Flow to Equity (FCFE)
description: Derives free cash flow to equity from FCFF by subtracting after-tax interest expense and adding net borrowing, FCFF - intexp*(1-t) + nb. It is the cash available to equity holders after servicing debt.
notes: t is the tax rate as a decimal, and nb is net borrowing (new debt minus repayments); negative net borrowing reduces FCFE. Keep all figures in the same currency and period.

cat: Capital budgeting and cost of capital
name: Terminal Value (Perpetuity Growth)
description: Computes the terminal value of a cash-flow stream using the Gordon growth model, the next-year cash flow divided by the discount rate less the growth rate, FCF*(1+g)/(r-g). It captures all value beyond the explicit forecast horizon.
notes: Requires r greater than g or the value becomes meaningless; g should be a modest long-run rate below the discount rate. FCF is the final explicit-year cash flow, grown one period.

cat: Capital budgeting and cost of capital
name: Internal Rate of Return (Two-Cashflow Approximation)
description: Computes the annualized internal rate of return for a single investment and single payoff as the compound annual growth rate, (FV/PV)^(1/n) - 1. It is the constant yearly rate that grows the present value into the future value.
notes: Valid only for one outflow and one inflow, not for multiple interim cash flows. PV and FV must be positive and in the same currency; n is the number of years.

cat: Capital budgeting and cost of capital
name: Net Present Value (Single Cash Flow minus Initial Outlay)
description: Computes the net present value of a single future cash flow CF received after n periods, discounted at rate r, minus the initial outlay C0: CF/(1+r)^n - C0. A positive result means the investment adds value at that discount rate.
notes: The rate r is a per-period decimal and n counts periods matching it. C0 is entered as a positive number and subtracted; only one future cash flow is modeled here.

cat: Capital budgeting and cost of capital
name: Payback Period (Even Cash Flows)
description: Computes the payback period C0/cf, the number of years needed to recover an initial investment C0 from a constant annual cash flow cf. It measures how quickly an outlay is recouped, ignoring the time value of money.
notes: Assumes equal cash flows each year; result is in years and may be fractional. It disregards discounting and any cash flows received after the payback point.

cat: Capital budgeting and cost of capital
name: After-Tax Cost of Debt
description: Computes the after-tax cost of debt rd*(1-t), the effective interest cost to a firm after the tax deductibility of interest, where rd is the pre-tax rate and t the tax rate. It is a key input to the weighted average cost of capital.
notes: Both rd and t are decimal fractions (0.06 = 6%). The tax shield reduces the effective cost only where interest is deductible; the result is always below the pre-tax rate for positive t.

cat: Capital budgeting and cost of capital
name: Equivalent Annual Annuity
description: Converts a project's net present value NPV into an equivalent level annual cash flow, NPV*r/(1-(1+r)^(-n)), spread over its life of n years at discount rate r. It puts projects of different durations on a comparable per-year basis.
notes: The rate r is the annual discount rate as a decimal and n is the project life in years. It is the reverse of present-value of an annuity; use it to rank projects with unequal lives.

cat: Capital budgeting and cost of capital
name: Accounting Rate of Return (ARR)
description: Computes the accounting rate of return as average annual profit divided by average investment. It expresses the expected annual accounting profit of a project as a fraction of the capital invested.
notes: It is based on accrual profit and ignores the time value of money, unlike IRR or NPV; the result is a decimal fraction (multiply by 100 for percent). Average investment is often taken as (initial + salvage) / 2.

cat: Capital budgeting and cost of capital
name: Net Present Value of a Cash-Flow List
description: Discounts a whole list of cash flows at rate r and adds them up; the first value is at time 0 (not discounted), the next one period later, and so on.
notes: Same convention as the textbook NPV. Spreadsheet NPV() assumes the first value is one period away, so add the time-0 flow separately there.

cat: Capital budgeting and cost of capital
name: Internal Rate of Return of a Cash-Flow List
description: Finds the discount rate that makes the NPV of the cash flows zero.
notes: Assumes one sign change for a unique answer; with several sign changes there can be more than one IRR. Shown as a fraction (0.16 = 16 %).

cat: Capital budgeting and cost of capital
name: Modified Internal Rate of Return
description: Computes the MIRR: negative flows are discounted at the finance rate, positive flows compounded to the end at the reinvestment rate, and the rate linking the two is returned.
notes: Avoids the multiple-answer problem of IRR and the unrealistic assumption that proceeds are reinvested at the IRR itself.

cat: Capital budgeting and cost of capital
name: Discounted Payback Period
expression: sum(k, 1, len(cf) - 1, sum(j, 0, k - 1, at(cf, j + 1) / (1 + r)^j) < 0)
description: Counts the whole periods before the cumulative discounted cash flow turns non-negative.
notes: Unlike the simple payback period it respects the time value of money. Returns the number of periods still under water; the investment pays back during the next one.

cat: Capital budgeting and cost of capital
name: Present Value of Uneven Cash Flows

variables.label: Cash flows at the end of periods 1, 2, …

description: Discounts a list of future cash flows, the first one period from now, back to today.
notes: This is what spreadsheet NPV(rate; values) computes.

cat: Capital budgeting and cost of capital
name: Future Value of Uneven Cash Flows
expression: sum(k, 1, len(cf), at(cf, k) * (1 + r)^(len(cf) - k))

variables.label: Deposits at the end of periods 1, 2, …

description: Compounds a list of end-of-period deposits forward to the end of the last period.
notes: The last deposit earns no interest; the first earns n − 1 periods of it.

cat: Capital budgeting and cost of capital
name: Capitalised Cost
description: Gives the present value of owning something forever: first cost plus the perpetuity of its annual cost.
notes: Used in engineering economy to compare long-lived public projects.

cat: Capital budgeting and cost of capital
name: Arithmetic Gradient Present Worth
description: Values a cash flow that is 0 at period 1 and rises by G each period (G, 2G, … at periods 2, 3, …): the (P/G, i, n) factor.
notes: Add the ordinary annuity for the base amount to value a series such as 1000, 1100, 1200 and so on.

cat: Capital budgeting and cost of capital
name: Arithmetic Gradient Uniform Series
description: Converts an arithmetic gradient G into the equivalent level payment per period: the (A/G, i, n) factor.
notes: For G = 100 over 10 periods at 6 % the level equivalent is about 402.2.

cat: Capital budgeting and cost of capital
name: Levered Beta (Hamada)
description: Converts an unlevered (asset) beta to the equity beta at a given debt-to-equity ratio.
notes: Used to take a peer group's beta and apply it to a company with a different capital structure.

cat: Capital budgeting and cost of capital
name: Unlevered Beta (Hamada)
description: Removes the effect of debt from an equity beta to get the beta of the business itself.
notes: Assumes debt carries no market risk (debt beta zero).

cat: Capital budgeting and cost of capital
name: Net Operating Profit after Tax (NOPAT)
description: Gives the operating profit a company would earn after tax if it had no debt.
notes: The numerator of ROIC and EVA.

cat: Capital budgeting and cost of capital
name: Return on Invested Capital (ROIC)
description: Divides NOPAT by the capital invested in operations (debt plus equity, less excess cash).
notes: A company creates value when ROIC exceeds its WACC.

cat: Capital budgeting and cost of capital
name: Economic Value Added (EVA)
description: Subtracts a charge for all the capital used from NOPAT; positive EVA means profit above the cost of capital (Stern Stewart).

cat: Capital budgeting and cost of capital
name: Market Value Added (MVA)

variables.label: Market value of debt and equity

description: Gives the wealth a company has created for investors: market value minus the capital they put in.
notes: In theory it equals the present value of all future EVA.

cat: Capital budgeting and cost of capital
name: Cost of Equity (Dividend Growth Model)
description: Estimates the return shareholders require from the dividend yield plus expected dividend growth.
notes: Rearranged Gordon growth model; sensitive to the growth assumption.

cat: Capital budgeting and cost of capital
name: Cost of Equity with Flotation Costs
description: Gives the cost of newly issued equity, which is higher than that of retained earnings because of issuing costs.
notes: Here 9.42 % against 9.2 % without flotation costs.

cat: Capital budgeting and cost of capital
name: Cost of Preferred Stock
description: Divides the fixed preferred dividend by the net price received.
notes: No tax adjustment, since preferred dividends are not deductible.

cat: Capital budgeting and cost of capital
name: Modigliani–Miller Value of a Levered Firm
description: Adds the present value of the perpetual interest tax shield t·D to the value of the unlevered firm (MM 1963).
notes: Ignores costs of financial distress, which limit borrowing in practice.

cat: Capital budgeting and cost of capital
name: Modigliani–Miller Cost of Equity
description: Gives the cost of equity rising with leverage: r_E = r_U + (r_U − r_D)(1 − t)D/E (MM proposition II with taxes).

cat: Capital budgeting and cost of capital
name: Adjusted Present Value (APV)
description: Values a project as its all-equity NPV plus the present value of the interest tax shields of permanent debt.
notes: Suits leveraged buyouts and projects whose debt changes over time.

cat: Capital budgeting and cost of capital
name: Merger EPS Accretion/Dilution
description: Compares the combined company's EPS with the acquirer's stand-alone EPS; positive means accretive.
notes: Accretion alone does not prove a deal creates value.

cat: Capital budgeting and cost of capital
name: Share Exchange Ratio
description: Gives the number of acquirer shares given for each target share in a stock deal.
notes: Here 0.75 acquirer shares per target share.

cat: Capital budgeting and cost of capital
name: Acquisition Premium
description: Gives how far the offer price exceeds the target's share price before the deal was known.
notes: Typical public takeovers carry premiums of 20–40 %.
